note: Patterns that map the compiler's first error to a class of the model's CheckError, tried in order. A failed instantiation's first error carries the note of the constraint that failed. 'has no attribute 'copy'' comes before unknownAttribute: the compiler reports .copy() of a value that is not Copyable as a missing attribute, the model as notCopyable. 'has no attribute' is the compiler's error for an unknown field and for an unknown method alike, on any type. 'does not designate a value with an origin', the compiler's error for moving an element out of a list or an array, comes before escapingReference, whose pattern also matches 'origin'. 'use of invalidated interior reference' is the compiler's error for a reference to a list element used after the list changed. 'is uninitialized at (the implicit )?return from this function', the compiler's error for a 'mut' parameter or the 'self' of '__init__' left partly uninitialized when the function returns, comes before uninitializedUse, whose pattern also matches 'uninitialized'. 'invalid use of mutating method on rvalue' is the compiler's error for a 'mut self' method called on a value that cannot be changed, such as 'p^' or a 'read' parameter, and 'value passed to mutable argument ... must be mutable' its error for such a value passed to a 'mut' parameter; the model reports both as immutablePlace. In the subset, only a struct that holds a list or an array of itself has a field of a non-'Deinitable' type. 'does not conform to trait 'Writable'' is the compiler's error for printing a value that print cannot write. 'no matching function in initialization' is the compiler's error for every initialization whose arguments fit no initializer: a construction with wrong arguments, a literal that does not fit the list or array it initializes, and List[T](...) with arguments; it is matched whole, so that no other message reaches noMatchingInit.
